clue.text: Used to back worker

parts.note: to back someone is to second them, offering support
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand or deckhand

explanation.surface: Someone used as a mere means of supporting a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are used have had a previous owner, which is what the compound adjective means.

clue.text: Oriental king's festival

parts.note: Oriental means of the East, the compass direction
ER, Edwardus Rex, is a royal cipher for a king; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: An Eastern monarch's celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of the Resurrection is one of the church's chief festivals.

clue.text: It's done to execute project

parts.note: when something is done and finished, it's over
to execute by the noose is to hang

explanation.surface: Something carried out in order to complete a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun (a scheme) but is the verb, pronounced pro-JECT: to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To jut out beyond what lies beneath is the verb sense of overhang.

clue.text: Some French to race when this goes off…

parts.note: de is French for 'of' or 'some', as in du pain
a race is a people, a nation

explanation.surface: A French phrase about a race, leading into a bomb going off in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 5 Down's surface; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosion is the moment a bomb or charge goes off.

clue.text: …but Nat Dean may be slow

indicators.note: 'may be' hints that the letters of Nat Dean may be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing from 4 Down: a man called Nat Dean might be sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Small coin 'or obscure note

parts.note: obscure means dim, faint and hard to make out
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A little coin, or else a note whose meaning is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: A US ten-cent piece is a small coin.

clue.text: Wild boar actually existing among the trees

indicators.note: wild signals that the letters of boar run riot into a new order

parts.note: something actually existing is real, not imaginary

explanation.surface: A wild pig that genuinely lives in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes creatures living in trees, such as squirrels and monkeys.

clue.text: Temple destroyed in Lear? Can't be

indicators.note: destroyed signals that the words Lear and can't be are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A temple wrecked in King Lear? Surely not.
explanation.definitionFit: The portable sanctuary of the Israelites, and any place of worship, is called a tabernacle.

clue.text: I meet a secret policeman in the peninsula

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD

explanation.surface: Encountering a Soviet spy chief somewhere in southern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass holding Spain and Portugal is the Iberian Peninsula, known by this name.

clue.text: When enraptured the" man agreed

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
sent is old slang for enraptured, carried away (that music sends me)
Ed, short for Edward, is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man said yes while in a state of rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to consent or say yes, so the past tense means agreed.

clue.text: The account for a decent round trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of a decent fall into a new order

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: The bill for a respectable return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round trip' looks like one phrase, a return journey; split it, so 'round' gives O and 'trip' signals the anagram of A DECENT plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: A short story or account told about a real incident is an anecdote.

clue.text: Yard measure

definitions.meaning: a yard is an enclosed open space beside a building
a measure of the size of a surface, in square units

explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard is an open space or region, and the extent of a surface is its size in square units.

clue.text: "---s cropped up like hay" (Gilbert)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: W. S. Gilbert's song 'There lived a King' in The Gondoliers lists diplomats springing up as plentifully as hay

explanation.walkthrough: The full line runs 'Ambassadors cropped up like hay, Prime Ministers and such as they grew like asparagus in May'; the dash is the singular word to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank in Gilbert's line is filled by the title of a top-ranking diplomat sent abroad.

clue.text: Digger makes a point with the administrative officer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed (scan confirms): 'Digger makes a point with the administrative officer (10)'. A + N + TIP + O + DEAN needs an O no clue word supplies, and ANTIPODE (a point) + DEAN would share DE; no complete parse found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Digger makes a point with the administrative officer

clue.text: Criticize Dutchman over instrument — the pompous ass

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first pieces above the next one

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticize it harshly
Jan is a common Dutch man's name
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: Attack a Dutch fellow over his musical instrument and call him a pompous fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-important official who puts on airs is mocked with this invented word from Samuel Foote.

clue.text: Snip to stop growth

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
gain means growth or increase

explanation.surface: A cut made to halt something growing, as in pruning.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a snip is something bought cheaply, a good deal.

clue.text: Slipped back to fall into debt

indicators.note: into puts the word for fall inside the word for debt

parts.note: in the red means in debt, so red stands for debt
a lapse is a fall or decline

explanation.surface: Someone sank back into old ways and ran up debts.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into an earlier, worse state, such as illness or a bad habit.

clue.text: Strange licensee — a bit innocent

indicators.note: a bit signals that only a portion of the words strange licensee is used, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: An odd publican who is somewhat naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being saintly and pure as a heavenly being, the adjective describes innocence.

clue.text: Adopts a couple in a German town

indicators.note: in places the word for a couple inside the town's name

parts.note: Ems, or Bad Ems, is a spa town in western Germany
a brace is a pair, said especially of game birds

explanation.surface: A pair living in a German town take on a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up an idea or cause wholeheartedly is to adopt it, a figurative sense of hug.

clue.text: Floor where this residence is?

definitions.meaning: to floor someone is to knock them down level with the ground
a playful address: the word split as a home and a number, flat number 10

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the word as an address, a flat (residence) numbered 10, with the question mark admitting the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock down level is to floor, and split in two the word is an address, a home numbered 10.

clue.text: Fish girl is the cause of food poisoning

parts.note: a salmon is a fish
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's fish dinner made someone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: This bacterium, found in undercooked meat and eggs, is a common cause of gastric infection.

clue.text: Sad waste

definitions.meaning: low in spirits, down in the dumps
an old British slang verb for squandering money, as with a windfall

explanation.definitionFit: The colour word also means low-spirited, and in British slang means to spend money recklessly.

clue.text: Dangerous for Peter to support international organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
peter is old criminal slang for a strongbox; a peterman is a safebreaker

explanation.surface: Risky for a man named Peter to back the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name but is underworld slang for a strongbox; 'to support' puts it below UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is perilous or risky is not secure.

clue.text: Two Greek characters abandoning a literary set

parts.note: alpha leads the Greek letters

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter a is dropped from the pair of Greek letters

parts.note: beta is the second Greek letter

explanation.surface: Two Greeks walking out on a group of writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literary' is used in its root sense of 'to do with letters', so the set is a set of letters; 'a' is the letter dropped from the end of the second Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The full series of letters used to write a language is a set of letters, which is what literary hints at.

clue.text: It's right to polish up rough pronunciation

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for polish reads upwards, back to front

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it

explanation.surface: A correct way to smooth out coarse speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled, guttural R in speech, as in some rural English and Scottish accents, is called this.

clue.text: Unfortunately can't rout the renegade

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of can't rout get jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly the defector cannot be routed.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor who switches sides is a renegade.

clue.text: Hobbs or Sutcliffe, possibly, was more frank

definitions.meaning: Jack Hobbs and Herbert Sutcliffe were England's celebrated pair of first batsmen in 1920s cricket

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the batsmen who go in first, like Hobbs and Sutcliffe for England, begin the innings; 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who starts the innings is this, and someone more candid is more open.

clue.text: Circus boss to double round the pole

indicators.note: round places the word for double around the word for the pole

parts.note: a ringer is a double or lookalike, as in dead ringer
a mast is a tall pole, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A circus manager made to go twice around the tent pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The person directing acts in the big top is the circus's master of ceremonies.
